description: The line plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES and Random—in predicting human trajectories, measured by the minimum FDE₂₀ (minFDE₂₀) metric, as a function of the number of training examples. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," ranges from 0 to 8 and is marked with integer values at intervals of 2, representing the number of training examples used for prediction. The y-axis, labeled "minFDE₂₀ (←)," represents the minimum final displacement error, with values ranging from 0.21 to 0.24 and tick marks at intervals of 0.01; a lower value indicates better performance. The ST-ES method is represented by a blue line with circular markers, which starts at a high minFDE₂₀ of approximately 0.242 when using 0 examples, then drops sharply to about 0.211 at 1 example, and fluctuates slightly between 0.209 and 0.212 for the remaining data points. The Random method is represented by an orange line with circular markers, which begins at a minFDE₂₀ of approximately 0.231 at 0 examples, decreases to about 0.224 at 1 example, and then shows minor fluctuations, remaining between 0.221 and 0.227 across the rest of the range.
